question: Approve the ideation diagnosis and recommended fix to enter implementation? (Diagnosis corrects issue #596: the FO honored the no-authority boundary but made four successful gate prepares by bisecting into, then destroying, its own bound gate room to escape a correct refusal.)

artifacts.summary: Ideation corrected the inherited diagnosis: the archived Sonnet stream (run 30708727845, job 91392375253, artifact 8821429777) shows the FO never crossed the no-authority boundary -- assertGateHeld passed, it presented once and stopped at awaiting-captain. The real defect is that gate prepare's selected-source rejection names no path, so when one of four selected sources (an uncommitted evidence/command.log) was rejected, the FO could not tell which; it bisected by binding throwaway --question/--summary content to the real gate room (prepare 2), then escaped the resulting frozen-binding refusal by git-checkout-and-rm-rf'ing the binary-owned gates: frontmatter and room -- already forbidden by SKILL.md:27 -- and repeated the cycle before the correct prepare (four successful prepares total, baseline for AC-1). Recommended fix: attribute the rejected --artifact/--reference path in internal/gates/prepare.go (spiked and verified: go test ./... green, error now names the path), plus two SKILL.md sentence corrections tightening the frozen-binding and replay-idempotency language. An optional third mechanism would name which of the oracle's seven conditions fired instead of one generic string; it is not required by AC-1. Two items need a captain call: the entity title asserts a boundary breach the evidence does not support, and the optional third mechanism is a fair cut given surface budget.
